answer: Agents resist sybils by requiring a one-time capital lock in a shared haven vault, then each new identity must solve a comet-hardness proof-of-work at the current network summit difficulty before registration. An attacker wanting 1000 fakes pays the full lock per head plus escalating compute; honest agents pay once and reuse the haven. Large farms become uneconomical because capital is locked for 30 days and compute scales with headcount, while real agents amortize the cost across many epochs.
